A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same similarity-consistency framework and corresponding empirical study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original representational-similarity analyses across 64 pretrained models and 23 datasets, linear-probe performance results, and supplementary sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains the original empirical study and adds bootstrap, dataset-subgroup, and training-domain results in Appendices C, H, and I.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the framework: extract representations, compute pairwise similarities, correlate similarity vectors across datasets, and examine correlation distributions. The revised kernel bandwidth and sampling budgets concern evaluation settings; newly documented normalization does not establish a methodological change.

E1.justification: The same 23 downstream evaluation datasets remain. Appendix I adds models pretrained for scene recognition on Places365, extending training-domain coverage beyond the original general-purpose model collection. Natural versus non-natural stratification reuses existing evaluation datasets.

E2.justification: The reported comparison-model roster changes: Table 2 replaces vit-large-patch14-clip-224.laion2b with barlowtwins-rn50. Appendix I adds matched ImageNet/Places365 comparisons using AlexNet, DenseNet161, ResNet18, and ResNet50. The PDFs do not establish whether the Table 2 revision reflects rerunning experiments or correcting the inventory.

E3.justification: V1 uses RBF CKA with sigma=0.4 and a 10,000-sample cap for its local analyses. V2 uses sigma=0.2 with up to 30,000 samples, retaining 10,000 for linear CKA (Appendix C). New protocols separately analyze natural/non-natural datasets and compare four architectures under ImageNet versus Places365 pretraining while controlling objective and architecture/size categories.

E4.justification: V2 substantially extends the existing sensitivity analyses with bootstrap checks of stimulus-sampling stability, natural/non-natural subgroup robustness, and a controlled training-domain comparison (Appendices C, H, I). Appendix F expands local/global metric validation, and the anchor analysis now examines the more localized sigma=0.2 setting.

E5.justification: Appendix C newly reports 500 bootstrap iterations for six anchor models, displaying sampling distributions for linear CKA on 10,000 images and RBF CKA on 30,000 images (Fig. 12). This adds uncertainty estimation for the central similarity measurements. The existing three-seed averaging of linear-probe accuracy remains unchanged.

E6.justification: New results include higher consistency among Places365-trained pairs, natural/non-natural subgroup differences, and local/global ranking reversals (Figs. 16, 19, 20). Fig. 3 replaces the 0.98 linear/RBF correlation at sigma=0.4 with 0.85 at sigma=0.2, under different settings. The linear/RSA consistency correlation also changes from 0.68 to 0.69 (v1 Fig. 12; v2 Fig. 15).

T1.justification: The definitions of representations, similarity vectors, and cross-dataset correlation distributions remain mathematically equivalent. Neither version contains a theorem or proof that is added, removed, or substantively revised.

C1.justification: V1's contribution list groups training data with architecture and model size as not qualitatively meaningful factors. V2 removes training data from that dismissal and presents objective as a crucial factor. The framework, superior consistency of SSL models, and dataset-dependent relationship with performance remain central claims.

C2.justification: V2 limits weak training-data effects to large, diverse datasets and mainly dataset size. Appendix I distinguishes convergence to specialized solutions from general representations. Appendix F explains local/global differences through fine-grained classes and acknowledges that sigma=0.4 partly captures global structure. Appendix H adds explanations for natural/non-natural subgroup differences.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents L2 feature normalization, expands model and dataset provenance, adds a source column to Table 2, and provides weight sources for Appendix I. It clarifies ImageNet validation-set evaluation and states that data accompany the existing code release. These disclosures do not establish that normalization or the original evaluation split actually changed.

R1.justification: V2 adds Dwivedi and Roig and Borup et al. on similarity-based model selection, and engages Conwell et al. when motivating the training-domain analysis. Additional model/dataset references accompany expanded provenance, while discussion of formal metric requirements is shortened. The central positioning relative to the Platonic Representation Hypothesis remains.

P1.justification: V2 shortens the title, tightens prose, merges contribution bullets, updates affiliations, removes Author Contributions, and adds an Impact Statement. Appendix headings and explanations are expanded, but the main section sequence and most of the narrative remain recognizable.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column conference layout and extensively resizes and rearranges displays. Fig. 7 changes panel arrangement; Fig. 8 is condensed while v1's full plot survives as v2 Fig. 21. Tables are relocated or restructured, and new heatmaps, bootstrap plots, and controlled-comparison figures substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evidence for the paper's central conclusions. Bootstrap checks and the more localized RBF analysis improve validation of sampling reliability and metric robustness (Appendices C, F). The ImageNet/Places365 comparison directly tests training-domain effects and corrects v1's overly broad dismissal of training data (Appendix I; Section 4.5). These gains outweigh the reduced readability of some smaller main-text figures, although model-attribute confounding still limits causal conclusions.
